title: Tension at equilibrium
description: Essential: The final answer for part (1) must be expressed as T = √2 mg or an equivalent numerical form.

title: Electric force relation
description: Important: The solution must correctly relate the electric field force to the weight using the equilibrium condition at 45°, establishing qE = mg.

title: Potential energy change sign
description: Essential: For part (2), the answer must state the electric potential energy increases and provide the correct magnitude, e.g., (2-√2)mgL/2.

title: Work-energy application (A to P)
description: Important: The calculation for part (2) must correctly apply the work done by the electric force over the horizontal displacement from A to P.

title: Final speed at P
description: Essential: The final answer for part (3) must provide the speed at point P in a correct form, such as √(2√2 gL).

title: Energy conservation from B
description: Important: For part (3), the solution must use energy conservation (work-energy theorem) from release point B to the lowest point C, accounting for both gravity and the electric field.

title: Velocity component analysis
description: Important: After finding the speed at C, the solution must correctly resolve the velocity component perpendicular to the string to find the speed at P.

title: Sign error in force direction
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the electric force direction is reversed in the force balance or energy equations, leading to incorrect signs or magnitudes.

title: Unit or expression omission
description: Pitfall: Penalize if final answers are given as pure numbers without the required physical quantities (mg, gL, etc.) or necessary square roots.
